design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A retired man rings to say he cannot drive and would like his mother's brooch posted to him when the bench has finished with it. That is the whole request. Answering it correctly means noticing that the workshop is not allowed to have gone near the piece yet - it is carried above the level's stone release threshold and the release has never been signed - and that the postage is banded on the value the release names, not on the guess written down at the counter. The difficulty is in reading one prerequisite sentence, seeing from the record that the state it waits on does not hold, working out from an estate appraisal, a protection plan and the order's own history what the piece is properly held at, handing that step to the customer, and only then pricing a postage line off ten tiered rules across four registers.

SCOPE: ALREADY OCCUPIED, THIS TASK, RESERVED. Task 0 occupied service_ext_claim_coverage_credit, service_ext_revised_authorization and service_ext_expedited_surcharge, with the subjects service_coverage_applied, service_work_authorized and service_rush_fee_charged and the three tools that serve them. This task claims the two that were deliberately left: service_ext_carried_release_value on service_order_details_updated (tool confirm_stone_release_3a8d360e) and service_ext_insured_return_shipping on service_shipping_charged (tool charge_insured_shipping_16f801d8). The two scopes are disjoint in policy, in tool, in subject and in governing base policy - task 0's lineage runs to service_protection_coverage, service_authorization and service_expedited_handling, this one's to service_intake_admission and service_settlement. With M = 2 nothing is reserved beyond this task, and the difficulty's five policies are exactly the union of the two scopes.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED. `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/workshop_service_desk --tasks 2` printed for this task {"task": 1, "key": "fine_jewelry_retailer/workshop_service_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 6]}. The tree therefore has one prerequisite problem, and the two computations carry four and six factors: the release value took 4 and the postage took 6.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: service_ext_insured_return_shipping - the postage the customer rang about. The single edge: service_ext_insured_return_shipping waits on service_ext_carried_release_value. Kind value_input, gate the compute binding `carried_value`, form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the root's own rule: 'The charge for sending the piece back is worked out only after the work order carries a signed release naming the value the piece is held at.' Four-point test: the ordering connective is 'only after'; the side it waits on is a record-visible state - a signed release standing on the work order with the value it names - and not an action or a performer; it names no tool, no policy id and no snake_case or hexadecimal token; and its strength matches the edge exactly, a hard requirement over one state of one order. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: confirm_stone_release_3a8d360e is the only tool that touches a work order's release or the value standing on it, and only service_ext_carried_release_value targets it. Derivation the reader performs: the sentence says the postage waits on a signed release naming the value; the work order shows the release unsigned and only the counter figure standing; the release policy's own rule says the release a customer signs names the value the chain carries the piece at and that the value is worked out from the papers on the piece; therefore the release must be signed first, and the figure it names is what that policy computes. Handling-time state (condition): the work order shows the release signed and carries the value the piece is held at. Resolving action: confirm_stone_release_3a8d360e, owner=user. There is one edge, so the order is forced and no parallel pair needs proving commutative. The seed evidence that the edge is false at the opening and the deletion run are recorded in prerequisite_closure.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Subject service_order_details_updated is governed by service_intake_admission alone. That policy's only structured gate, stone_release_on_file, is scoped to the taking-in of a piece and not to a correction of a running order, so no gate is inherited for this write and the precondition is declared as policy_scope; the policy's other clauses are inherited and satisfied item by item - the level's ceiling on declared value is 100000.00 and the value written is far below it, the level admits antique and estate restoration, the level does not require a designer's authorisation, and photographs are required at this level and were taken at intake. Subject service_shipping_charged is governed by service_settlement alone. Its gate payable_state applies to this subject and is satisfied: the order stands in_workshop, one of the four states in which money may be moved against an order, and the gate's correlation key is the work order reference, which the call passes as its own argument. The rest of that policy is inherited: insured shipping is charged per leg at the level's rate, and the declared value shipped, 13888.00, is well inside the level's shipping insurance ceiling of 50000.00, so the piece may be sent rather than held for collection - which matters, because the level does not allow anyone but the customer to collect. No time-kind eligibility gate exists in either lineage, which is why temporal_feasibility is empty.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is work order WO-503284, the only running order this customer has; WO-488120 closed as delivered on 2026-02-20 and is excluded by its status and its reference. The correlation key the postage line carries is that work order reference, written onto the call itself. Rows entering the aggregates: the insured leg of 55.00 and the payment of 2100.00, both on WO-503284. Rows excluded: the February order's resizing, its insured leg of 18.00 and its payment - and the insured leg is the standing trap, because a count of insured legs taken across the customer rather than across the order reaches two and selects the frequent-leg step. The appraisal and the coverage are both matched to the piece by its own item reference, BRCH-19044, not by the customer, so neither can be confused with anything else in the file.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The unsigned release and the counter figure of 6800.00 on the order are the prerequisite itself; sign the release in the seed and the whole tree collapses to one problem. The desk's request record carrying the release consent as recorded rather than confirmed is the corroborating system evidence that it was asked for and never given. The insured leg of 55.00 is the second factor of the postage and the natural reason the brooch is at a bench a thousand miles from its owner; the payment of 2100.00 is the second limb of the holding step in the release value. The appraisal engagement carries the value the release rests on and the currency that decides both the evidenced share of the cover cap and the paperwork step. The protection plan carries the standing, the settled-claim count and the price the covered piece was sold at, which decide the cover step and the value band. The membership and its ledger carry the qualifying workshop spend of 2100.00 inside twelve months, the older 640.00 outside it (the near-miss: counting it reaches 2740.00 and wrongly selects the high relief), and the complimentary appraisal drawn in March that decides how the relief is applied. The February order and its three entries are the excludable distraction. Automatic clauses checked row by row: no storage charge can have arisen, because the piece has never been completed and the level's sixty-day holding period has not begun; abandonment is likewise unreachable; the February order's guarantee ran out on 2026-08-20 so no rework obligation stands; and no cache field is read by either computation - the order's balance_due of -1960.00 agrees with its entries, so this task sets no cache trap.

PERSONA DESIGN. Franklin is deliberately the opposite of task 0's caller in voice and pace: older, methodical, unhurried, assuming there is a proper procedure. Volunteered at the opening: the brooch, his mother's death, the end-of-August intake, the knee and the request to have it posted - each supported by the seed (intake_date 2026-08-31, the order at the Heritage bench). Given only when asked: his name, the number the store has for him, his date of birth, the last four of his identification, that he cannot quote a work order number, that the estate had the piece valued but the figure is at home, and that the brooch is on a Belrose plan and he holds a card. Reacted to only after the agent speaks: he asks what figure the release will name before agreeing, carries out that step himself once it is handed over and repeats back what it says, accepts the postage figure when told it, and closes once told the postage has been put on the order. His refusal to read the appraisal figure out is deliberate: the value gold writes must come from the chain's own record, never from the caller, and he says so in his own words. No line of his names a piece of work beyond the postage.

THE PREREQUISITE CHAIN AND WHY IT CANNOT BE REORDERED. Surface goal (post it to me) -> the postage is the level's rate with a value band on it -> the band is decided on the value standing on the order -> the order carries only the counter figure because the release has never been signed -> the release must be signed first, and the figure it names is itself computed from the appraisal, the coverage and the order's own history. Depth is two hops; breadth is genuinely parallel: the release value reads the appraisal register, the protection register, a date span and the order's payments, and the postage reads the protection register, the appraisal register, the loyalty register, the order's shipping history and two date spans against two different turnarounds of the same level.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT. Pricing the postage at the level's bare rate of 55.00 is what an agent gets who finds the computation document and none of the factor documents. Banding the postage on the 6800.00 standing at intake is the trap the tree is built on, excluded by the root's own prerequisite sentence. Counting the February order's insured leg reaches two legs and the wrong step; every sentence speaks of legs standing on the work order. Counting the 2025 workshop accrual toward the twelve-month spend reaches 2740.00 and selects the high relief; the window is stated as the twelve months to the handling date. Measuring the promise against the level's rush turnaround rather than its target turnaround selects the express step; the rule states both and which one each tier reads. Taking the appraisal's 12400.00 as the carried value without the cover and holding steps gives 12400.00; taking the counter figure with the steps gives 7616.00. Each is excluded by a sentence that is quoted in compute_basis.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by the number and the name; verify on the date of birth and the last four of the identification; read the work orders and take WO-503284; read the ledger and separate the brooch's three entries from the February order's; read the request record and see the release consent standing recorded; read the coverage, the protection register, the appraisal engagement and its ledger, the membership and its ledger. Compute the release value: basis 12400.00 from the current estate report, plus the reduced cover step of 8 and the standing holding step of 4, giving 12400.00 x 1.12 = 13888.00, inside the whole cover cap of 100000.00. Hand the release to the customer and have him sign it. Compute the postage: 55.00 x (100 + 45 value band + 18 promise + 12 paperwork - 15 return leg) / 100 = 88.00, relieved by the standing member relief of 12 per cent taken off the whole charge, giving 77.44. Price it onto the order against reference WO-503284.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The same harness used for task 0, built on skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py (build_env / eval_compute / substitute), was run over this initial_state with the release write simulated before the postage was evaluated. Output: carried release value result=13888.0 (whole baseline 6800.0; per-factor baselines 7616.0 / 12896.0 / 13392.0 / 10000.0); insured return shipping result=77.44 (whole baseline 55.0; per-factor baselines 55.66 / 84.7 / 68.73 / 71.63 / 88.0 / 81.4). No factor left its result unchanged and neither whole baseline equalled gold. The prerequisite-sensitivity run with the release write skipped gave 65.34 for the postage. check_compute reproduces all of these against computations.expected and the gold arguments.

TWO-WAY SWEEP RULE <-> COMPUTE. Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim quotation - the two cross-category reads of the appraisal register, the three of the protection register, the two of the loyalty register, the count of payments, the count of insured legs, the two date spans in each policy, the six ladders, the cap and the roundings. Backward: every sentence of either rule that carries a quantity, a window, a filter, a branch, a cap or a rounding is claimed by a binding. Semantic choices are pinned in prose where they exist: the release value states that the steps are added together and applied once to the basis figure, and that the cover cap is compared after that, not before; the postage states that the value, promise and paperwork steps are added to the level's rate and the travelled-leg step taken off it before the relief is considered, and that which base the relief acts on is itself what the relief-application rule decides. The level's target and rush turnarounds are both stated to be counted in calendar days at five working days to the week, because the parameters are in business days and the comparisons are not.

OVERRIDES DECLARED AGAINST BASE. Both of this task's policies compute a quantity base also speaks to, so each names the base sentence it supersedes. service_ext_carried_release_value supersedes service_intake_admission's 'the declared value is what the chain answers for while the piece is in its care', because the extended rule fixes that figure from the papers standing on the piece rather than treating the counter figure as given; the same policy's ceiling on declared value, its restoration and designer clauses and its stone release gate all stay in force and are inherited. service_ext_insured_return_shipping supersedes service_settlement's 'Insured shipping is charged per leg at the level's rate', because the extended charge steps that rate by the value band, the promise, the papers and the leg already travelled before the member relief is applied; the rest of that sentence - that the declared value shipped never exceeds the level's shipping insurance ceiling - is deliberately not quoted and stays in force, and so does the payable_state gate, which this task inherits and declares. No base parameter value is changed: the level's own shipping rate, its turnarounds and its cover cap are read as base states them.

POLICY / GT CLOSURE. service_ext_carried_release_value -> confirm_stone_release_3a8d360e -> computations[0].carried_value -> action 12 -> the work order shows the release signed and carries 13888.00. service_ext_insured_return_shipping -> charge_insured_shipping_16f801d8 -> computations[1].shipping_amount -> action 14 -> an insured postage line of 77.44 on WO-503284. charter_scope.extended_policies equals the set of computations.policy_id, required_documents repeats it in order, and charter_scope.task_tools lists the two tools in first-call order. Across the difficulty the two tasks' scopes are disjoint and together cover all five extended policies.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this rationale masked, and working only from the published rules, the tool schemas, what the finders return and the caller's own lines: he wants it posted; the shipping document says the charge is the level's rate with the steps that bear on the leg added and the step for a leg already travelled taken off, and that it is worked out only after the order carries a signed release naming the value the piece is held at; the order shows the release unsigned and only the intake figure standing; the release document says that value is the basis figure from the papers on the piece with the cover and holding steps added, capped at the evidenced share of the cover cap. Re-derived that way the two figures were 13888.00 and 77.44, identical to gold. The one alternative reading considered - banding the postage on the price the covered piece was sold at rather than on the value standing on the order - is excluded by the wording of the value-band tiers, which name the value the piece is held at on one side of the comparison and the sold price on the other.

REVISIONS. (1) Symptom: check_solvability would reject the postage write, because the payable_state gate binds its correlation key service_orders.work_order_reference to an action argument of the same name and the tool had none. Root cause: the tool was written with the internal order reference alone. Change: charge_insured_shipping_16f801d8 now takes work_order_reference as a fixed-format argument, documents it as the reference standing on the work order, and folds it into the entry's own id; the gold call, the tracing and the evidence bindings were updated in the same pass. Re-run: the tool contract gate and the solvability gate both pass. (2) Symptom: the member relief factor sat on its top tier, which made the older workshop accrual useless as a near-miss. Root cause: the programme threshold was below the spend already booked inside the window. Change: the threshold was raised above the in-window spend and the older accrual was moved to 2025-08-14, just outside the twelve months, so that counting it flips the tier; the factor trace and this dossier record the near-miss. Re-run: the relief sits on the standing tier and the factor still moves the result. (3) Symptom: both policies computed a quantity base also provides for, with overwrite left empty, and the release rule additionally stated an ordering ('the release a customer signs before the bench handles a piece') that grounds no declared edge and merely repeats base. Root cause: an undeclared divergence and a redundant cross-problem ordering clause. Change: each policy now declares the base clause it supersedes; the release sentence was reworded to 'the release a customer signs for a piece the bench has in hand', in the rule and in the baseline paragraph together, so the only ordering sentence in this difficulty's extended rules is the one prerequisite sentence that grounds the edge. Re-run: every gate passes and both scored figures are unchanged. (4) Round-2 rework against the policy-task audit, items bearing on this task. F-4 / T1-2: the shipping rule no longer speaks of 'a finished piece' - it reads 'Sending a piece at the bench back to its owner insured', in the rule, the baseline paragraph, the compute basis and the override replacement together - so the act-now reading is the only one the wording invites; no figure changed. F-6: the tool docstrings lost their ordering words and the tracing quotations were updated to match. F-11: the two factors deciding their tier from the loyalty programme no longer carry cross_difficulty, since circle is no difficulty's product; the floor is met through the two protection factors, and the trace labels say cross-category. T1-1 is left as it stands: the appraisal ledger read confirms the engagement was issued and paid, a superset of the necessary read set and harmless. T1-3 and F-5 are observations carrying no consequence. Every scored figure of this task is unchanged at 13888.00 and 77.44. (5) Round-3: the published-KB audit returned PASS on both of this task's parts and recorded no finding against it - both of its computations are rounding-stable (12400.00 x 1.12 = 13888.00 and 55.00 x 1.60 = 88.00, then x 0.88 = 77.44, all exact at the cent under any convention), so B-1 does not reach this task. Nothing in this task's two policies was changed in that round; the source edits closing B-1 and the bench-total domain point are confined to service_ext_revised_authorization, which this task does not claim. Both scored figures stand at 13888.00 and 77.44.
user_scenario:
Franklin K. Osei-Boateng is sixty-eight and retired from the water district, and he talks the way a man does who spent thirty years reading meters and writing the numbers down: slowly, in order, one thing at a time. The brooch is his mother's. She died last spring, and of everything in the house it is the piece he means to keep - Edwardian, diamonds in platinum, with a run of the fine beaded edging gone from one side. He took it in to the Belrose store in Sacramento at the end of August and the restoration bench has had it since.

He telephones on a Friday afternoon about one thing only, and he says it plainly: "When it's finished I'd like it posted out to me rather than having to come in and collect it. I've had a knee replaced and I'm not driving for a while yet. Can that be arranged?" He is not in a hurry and he does not ask what anything costs; he assumes, as he would about a public utility, that there is a proper procedure and that someone will follow it.

He gives his name as Franklin K. Osei-Boateng, spelling the surname if he is asked to. For finding him on the system he offers the number the store has for him, 4155553352. If more is wanted before anything can be done on the account he gives his date of birth, 1957-11-09, and then, if that is still not enough, the last four digits of the identification the store copied when he first opened the account, 3318. He will not volunteer all of it at once; he answers what he is asked.

He can say what he knows and no more. He left the brooch at the end of August, a man at the counter went over it with a loupe and told him what it would take, he paid something towards it that day on his card, and he has not heard since. He does not have the paperwork in front of him and he cannot quote a work order number. If he is asked what he thinks the brooch is worth he says that his mother's estate had it valued after she died and that the figure is in a folder at home, but he will not read it out over the telephone and says the store will have its own record of it. If he is asked about coverage or about his Belrose card he confirms that the brooch has been on a Belrose plan since his mother bought it and that he has had a card himself for years, without being able to quote a number from either.

He is content for the desk to act for him where the desk normally would - "go ahead and do what's usual" - but anything with his name on it he wants explained first. If the agent tells him that before the bench can go any further he has to put his name to something that records what the brooch is held at while the chain has it, he asks what figure that will say, listens to the answer, and then agrees; when the agent passes that step across to him he does it himself and repeats back what it says. If he is told what the postage will come to he accepts it without argument - "that's fine, put it on the bill" - and asks nothing about how it was worked out.

Once the agent tells him the postage has been put on the order and the brooch will be sent out to him when the bench has finished, he is satisfied and says so. He thanks the agent for their patience and ends the call.

seed_consistency.check: An antique piece taken in at Heritage Restoration Service, the only level that both admits restoration work and carries a ceiling on declared value above what this piece is worth; it was taken in at 6800.00, above that level's stone release threshold of 5000.00, so a release was required before the bench could handle it - and the order shows it unsigned, which is why the piece sits at the bench untouched with no labour priced against it.

The February band was taken in at Standard Bench Service carried at 1450.00, below that level's stone release threshold of 2500.00, so no release was needed; it was priced, authorised, finished on 2026-02-17 and delivered on 2026-02-20, and its six-month workmanship guarantee ran out on 2026-08-20, before the handling date, so nothing on it is open.

The insured leg the brooch travelled in on, priced at the Heritage level's own insured shipping rate of 55.00 for one leg on 2026-09-01, the day after it was taken in; the value it travelled at is far below that level's shipping insurance ceiling of 50000.00.

The estimate charge of 85.00, which is the Heritage level's own estimate fee, booked as its own priced line under the estimate charge code on the day the estimate was prepared; at this level it is credited against the work when the customer goes ahead, which is why it stands as a line of its own rather than inside the bench pricing.
The deposit taken at the counter on the day the customer authorised the work: the Heritage level takes half of the authorised total above 500.00, and half of 4200.00 is 2100.00, taken in store.
The February resizing: one size up at the Standard level's per-size charge of 48.00 with that level's white gold surcharge taking it to 51.84, priced while that order stood in the workshop.

The insured leg that sent the band back in February, priced at the Standard level's own insured shipping rate of 18.00; it belongs to that order and not to the brooch's, which is exactly why it must be kept out of the count of legs on the live order.
The payment that cleared the February order in full on the day it was delivered - 51.84 of bench work and 18.00 of postage - which is why that order carries nothing owed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller matched the profile on two details he stated himself before anything is written against his work order.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A release is signed and a charge is priced on this order; neither may be written before the identity check stands recorded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull both work orders this customer has had and read the live one: the service level it runs at, its status, the value it was taken in at, whether the release has been signed, the piece it covers and the date it is promised back.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The service level fixes the shipping rate, the turnarounds and the cover cap; the value taken in at is the figure the release replaces; the promised date decides the promise step; the piece reference is what the coverage and the appraisal are matched on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every entry on both orders: the insured leg the brooch travelled in on, the estimate charge, the deposit, and the older band's own lines.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The count of insured legs already charged on this order decides the step taken off the rate, and the payment standing on the order is the second limb of the holding step; the older order's own insured leg is what must be kept out of that count.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the workshop desk's request record for this order and see the release consent standing merely recorded rather than confirmed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It is the plainest confirmation that the release the bench is waiting on has never been given.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the coverage on the brooch: its standing, the price the covered piece was sold at, and the claims settled against it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The standing and the settled-claim count decide the cover step in the value the release names; the standing and the sold price decide the value step in the shipping rate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read what has happened under that coverage: the allowance granted at the outset, the premium, the claim settled in 2019 and the inspection logged in January.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The settled claim is what puts the cover step on its reduced tier rather than the full one.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the appraisal engagement on the brooch: the value the report states, the day it runs to and where the engagement stands.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The report's value is the basis figure the carried value is built on, its currency decides the evidenced share of the cover cap, and its standing decides the paperwork step on the shipping rate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the fees and payment on that engagement to confirm the report was issued and settled rather than abandoned part way.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It is the check that the engagement genuinely reached a delivered report, which both the basis figure and the paperwork step rest on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the membership: the tier held and whether it stands active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The relief on the postage begins with whether the membership stands active.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the points history: the qualifying workshop spend booked inside the last twelve months, the older workshop spend outside it, and the benefit drawn in March.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The spend inside the window decides which relief rate applies, and the benefit drawn in the window decides how the relief is taken off.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the customer's own step for signing the release that names what the piece is held at, and hand it to him.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Putting his name to what the chain answers for on his own property is his to do; the desk can only work out the figure and pass the step across.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The customer signs the release himself, and the work order thereafter shows it signed and carries the value the brooch is held at while the chain has it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only this policy's computation produces that value, and the shipping charge below is banded on the value standing on the order.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_order_id: Value: the live work order row. Basis: the tool's contract says it is 'the reference number of the bench work order record the release is signed against, as returned by the work order lookup'. Uniqueness: the customer has one running order, WO-503284; the other, WO-488120, closed as delivered in February 2026, and nothing can be released against a closed order.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value: the profile reference returned by the customer lookup at step 0. Basis: the tool's contract says it is 'the reference number of the customer profile signing the release, as returned by the customer profile lookup'. Uniqueness: one profile matched the number and the name the caller stated, and the work order is held on it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.carried_value: Value: 13888.00, computed on the world as it stands before any write of this call. An appraisal report stands on this very piece - the estate appraisal issued on 2025-04-18 stating 12400.00 and current until 2028-04-18, well past the handling date - so the basis figure is the value that report states rather than the 6800.00 taken down over the counter. The coverage on the brooch stands active and one claim has already been settled against it, so the reduced cover step of 8 applies rather than the full step. The brooch has been in the chain's hands 25 days, which is inside the level's target turnaround of 25 business days (35 calendar days at five working days to the week), but a payment already stands on the order, so exactly one limb holds and the standing holding step of 4 applies. 12400.00 x 1.12 = 13888.00. The cover cap does not bind: a current report stands and the coverage stands in force, so the evidenced share is the whole of the level's care and custody cover cap, 100000.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's own action for pricing an insured postage leg onto a work order.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Price the insured postage onto the work order, which is what sets the brooch to travel out to the customer instead of being collected.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only this policy's computation produces the postage charge, and it is the write the customer's request points at.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_order_id: Value: the live work order row. Basis: the tool's contract says it is 'the reference number of the bench work order record the postage line is charged to, as returned by the work order lookup'. Uniqueness: only one of the customer's two orders is still at the bench and has a piece to send.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value: the profile reference returned by the customer lookup at step 0. Basis: the tool's contract says it is 'the reference number of the customer profile the work order belongs to, as returned by the customer profile lookup'. Uniqueness: the order is held on that one profile.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.work_order_reference: Value: WO-503284. Basis: the work order row carries it - initial_state.service_orders row field work_order_reference - and the tool's contract says the argument is 'the reference the customer is given for the work order the postage line is raised against ... copied exactly as it stands on the work order'. Uniqueness: the customer's only other reference, WO-488120, belongs to the order delivered in February; the caller himself cannot quote either, so the value can only come from the work order lookup.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.shipping_amount: Value: 77.44, computed on the world as it stands after the release has been signed and before this write. The level's own insured shipping rate is 55.00. The brooch is now held at 13888.00, at or above the 9600.00 the covered piece was sold at, and the coverage stands in force, so the upper value step of 45 is added. One insured leg already stands charged on this order - the 55.00 leg the brooch travelled in on, on 2026-09-01 - so the return-leg step of 15 is taken off; the 18.00 leg on the February order belongs to a different work order and is not counted. The brooch is promised back on 2026-10-16, 21 days from the handling date, which is outside the level's rush turnaround of 12 business days (16.8 calendar days) but inside its target turnaround of 25 business days (35 calendar days), so the standard promise step of 18 is added. The appraisal engagement on the piece stands delivered with a report current until 2028-04-18, so the report paperwork step of 12 is added. The rate is therefore 55.00 x (100 + 45 + 18 + 12 - 15) / 100 = 55.00 x 1.60 = 88.00. The membership stands active with 2100.00 of qualifying workshop spend inside the last twelve months, below the programme's threshold of 2500, so the relief is the standing relief of 12 per cent; a member benefit - the complimentary appraisal of 2026-03-02 - was drawn inside that window, so the relief is taken off the whole charge once every step has been applied: 88.00 x 0.88 = 77.44.

factor_trace: valuation_basis (method): the appraisal register carries an estate appraisal on this very piece, issued 2025-04-18, stating 12400.00 and current until 2028-04-18, which is 571 days past the handling date, so the first tier applies and the basis figure is the value the report states. The baseline takes the value the piece was taken in at, 6800.00, which would have carried the release value to 7616.00.

coverage_cover_step (parameter, cross-difficulty): the coverage on the brooch stands active with one claim already settled against it - the clasp claim settled on 2019-08-20 - so the reduced cover step of 8 applies rather than the full step of 15. The baseline step of nothing would have carried the release value to 12896.00.

holding_exposure_step (parameter): the brooch has been in the chain's hands 25 days, inside the level's target turnaround of 25 business days counted as 35 calendar days, but a payment of 2100.00 already stands on the order, so exactly one limb holds and the standing holding step of 4 applies. The baseline step of nothing would have carried the release value to 13392.00.

evidenced_ceiling_share (parameter): a current report stands on the piece and the coverage stands in force, so the evidenced share is the whole of the level's care and custody cover cap, 100000.00, which does not bind. The baseline narrow share would have capped the value at 10000.00.

bindings belonging to no factor: report_days_left reads the day the report runs to; stated_value applies the assembled steps to the basis figure; value_ceiling applies the evidenced share to the level's cover cap; result takes the lesser of the two and rounds it.

factor_trace: carried_value_band_step (parameter, cross-difficulty): the value now standing on the order, 13888.00, is at or above the 9600.00 the covered piece was sold at, and the coverage stands active, so the upper value step of 45 applies. The value standing on the order is what the prerequisite write brings into this calculation - before it the order read 6800.00, below the sold price, which selects the lower step of 20. The baseline step of nothing would have carried the charge to 55.66.

travelled_leg_step (parameter): exactly one insured leg already stands charged on this work order, the 55.00 the brooch travelled in on, so the return-leg step of 15 is taken off. The February order's own insured leg of 18.00 is the near-miss: counting it reaches two legs and wrongly selects the frequent-leg step. The baseline of no step would have carried the charge to 84.70.

promise_proximity_step (parameter): the brooch is promised back on 2026-10-16, 21 days from the handling date, outside the level's rush turnaround of 12 business days but inside its target turnaround of 25 business days, so the standard promise step of 18 applies. The baseline of no step would have carried the charge to 68.73.

travelling_papers_step (parameter): the appraisal engagement on the piece stands delivered and its report is current until 2028-04-18, so the report paperwork step of 12 applies. The baseline of no step would have carried the charge to 71.63.

member_shipping_relief_rate (parameter, cross-category): the membership stands active with 2100.00 of qualifying workshop spend inside the last twelve months, below the threshold of 2500, so the standing relief of 12 per cent applies. The workshop accrual of 640.00 dated 2025-08-14 is the near-miss outside the window - counting it reaches 2740.00 and wrongly selects the high relief. The baseline relief of nothing would have carried the charge to 88.00.

relief_application (method, cross-category): the membership stands active and one member benefit - the complimentary appraisal of 2026-03-02 - was drawn inside the twelve months, so the relief is taken off the whole charge once every step has been applied. The baseline takes it off the level's own rate alone and would have carried the charge to 81.40.
bindings belonging to no factor: covered_value and plan_status read the coverage; base_charge assembles the rate at 88.00; result rounds the relieved charge.

edges.condition: the work order shows the release signed and carries the value the piece is held at while the chain has it
edges.policy_source: The charge for sending the piece back is worked out only after the work order carries a signed release naming the value the piece is held at.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The work order shows the release unsigned, and the only value standing on it is the 6800.00 taken down over the counter at intake rather than a figure any signed release names. The workshop desk's own request record carries the release consent as merely recorded, never confirmed. Because 6800.00 is a real figure, an agent who never reads the prerequisite bands the postage on it and prices a confidently wrong charge rather than hitting an error.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's own signature marks the release signed on the work order and writes 13888.00 onto it as the value the piece is held at, so the order carries a signed release naming that value and the postage is banded on 13888.00 instead of 6800.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single edge, so there is only one order: the release is signed, then the postage is priced. Running the two the other way round was replayed in the Step 5 harness and gives 65.34 rather than 77.44, because the value band is decided on the counter figure of 6800.00, which sits below the 9600.00 the covered piece was sold at. No pair of parallel prerequisites exists to prove commutative.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the release leaves the value standing on the work order at 6800.00 instead of 13888.00, which puts the value band on its lower tier and recomputes the postage to 65.34 instead of 77.44; the terminal DB also keeps the release unsigned.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller names no prerequisite. He asks only that the finished brooch be posted out to him rather than collected, and gives his reason. He never mentions a release, a signature, a declared value or anything the chain must have before the bench can go further, and he drops no hint that something is outstanding. Asked what the brooch is worth he says only that the estate had it valued and that the figure is in a folder at home, and refers the desk to its own record - he does not read a number out and could not supply the one gold writes. Everything he contributes about the prerequisite comes after the agent has explained it: he asks what figure the release will say, listens, agrees, and then carries the step out himself when it is handed over.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither tool reads the state of the other problem. confirm_stone_release_3a8d360e rounds the figure it is given and calls ctx.update on the work order; charge_insured_shipping_16f801d8 computes an id and calls ctx.create on the ledger. Neither calls ctx.find, neither inspects a status, a release flag or a declared value, and neither can return an error: an agent who prices the postage before the release is signed gets a normal receipt and a wrong terminal hash.
